g.text: select starting bit offset (enter = use, esc = cancel)
Every reading agrees from bit 130; the rows differ only before it. The default start reads from there, so it shows only
what all of them agree on (now: bit 130). Choosing a row starts exactly there, and its first bytes are right only if that
Fewer holes can mean a wrong start: a start off a symbol boundary misreads a few bytes before it falls into step. ⊂N: a
tail of offset N's decode, which recovers less.
